steps.title: Apply online for your Canadian study permit (temporary resident visa included)
steps.why: Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study at a designated learning institution in Canada, and you should apply before you travel. Because your citizenship requires a visitor visa to enter Canada, IRCC issues the temporary resident visa together with your study permit approval — you don't apply separately or pay another fee, and the visa is placed in the passport you used to apply. Processing times vary by country, so submit as early as possible after accepting your UBC offer. Apply online through an IRCC secure account, which you also use to pay fees and check your application status. To apply you'll need a scanner or camera to make electronic copies of your documents and a valid credit or debit card. Before uploading forms, answer the online tool's questions to generate your personalized document checklist, read the instruction guide even though you're applying online, and check your local visa office instructions for the country you're applying from. (Paper applications from outside Canada are only for applicants with a disability that prevents online application, or who hold an identity/travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons.) After approval, travel with the passport you used to apply — your visa will be in it and shows whether you can enter Canada once or multiple times, and you must enter before the visa expires.
prerequisites: Accepted your UBC offer of admission
IRCC secure account created
Scanner or camera to create electronic copies of documents
Valid credit or debit card
Valid passport (the same one you travel with)
Local visa office instructions for the country you're applying from
steps.cost: CAD $150 study permit fee; no separate application or additional fee for the temporary resident visa issued with approval
steps.time_estimate: Processing times vary by country — check IRCC and apply as early as possible

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics (fingerprints and photo) within 30 days
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics for most study permit applications to confirm your identity and help assess your application. After you submit, IRCC sends a biometric instruction letter — you have 30 days to give your fingerprints and photo, and booking your collection appointment as soon as you can avoids processing delays. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted your online study permit application (with letter of acceptance and PAL/TAL)
Paid the biometrics fee when submitting your application
Received the letter from IRCC telling you to give biometrics
steps.cost: CAN$85 per individual applicant; maximum CAN$170 total for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Must be completed within 30 days of receiving the biometrics instruction letter

steps.title: Pay your Term 1 tuition from abroad by September 9, 2026
steps.why: Your Term 1 tuition fees for the Winter Session are due September 9, 2026. The first instalment covers tuition for Term 1 courses and the first half of two-term courses, plus most student fees. Because you're paying from outside Canada, start the transfer early enough that funds clear by the deadline — even on a straightforward major-currency corridor, bank wires take a few business days.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer of admission and paid the acceptance deposit through the Applicant Service Centre ($3,000 for students on a study permit)
Registered for your courses, so your specific fees are assessed
Checked your assessed fees under "Finances" in Workday
steps.cost: Varies by program — use the UBC cost estimator for an estimate, then confirm your exact assessed amount under "Finances" in Workday. Note your account will also be charged the temporary iMED medical insurance fee ($237, or $338 for one-term exchange students, plus a $10.54 direct billing fee) when you register for courses.
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to set up the transfer; initiate at least 1–2 weeks before September 9, 2026

steps.title: Prepare your port-of-entry documents and clear the border
steps.why: Your study permit is not issued until you arrive — a border services officer checks your documents and prints your permit at the port of entry. The letter of introduction IRCC sent you is not your study permit; without it (and the passport you applied with), the officer can't issue your permit.
prerequisites: Approved study permit application with a port of entry letter of introduction in your IRCC account
The same valid passport you used to apply for your study permit
A valid eTA (linked to that passport), valid visitor visa (temporary resident visa) in your passport, valid green card or equivalent proof of U.S. status, or another valid travel document
A copy of your valid UBC letter of acceptance (an updated LOA plus valid letter of introduction if you deferred enrolment)
Letters of reference or any other documents the visa office told you to bring
Proof of enough money for your stay
steps.time_estimate: 30–60 minutes to assemble documents; border screening on arrival varies

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) with Service Canada
steps.why: A SIN is the 9-digit number you need to work in Canada, open most types of bank accounts, and access government programs and benefits — so you must have one before starting any on-campus or off-campus job. As a temporary resident, your SIN starts with "9" and expires with your immigration documents, so note the expiry and reapply to extend it when you renew your study permit. Applying online gives faster processing. Your SIN is private and confidential — it is illegal for anyone else to use it, and a stolen SIN can lead to identity theft or loss of benefits, so protect it as soon as it is issued.
prerequisites: Be 12 years or older (anyone 12+ can apply for their own SIN)
One primary identity document proving your legal status in Canada (e.g. your immigration document)
One secondary identity document confirming your identity
Supporting documents if your name has changed, and translations if a document is not in English or French
Documents free of errors — if there is a mistake, contact the issuing source to correct it before applying (a mistake or missing document in your application means submitting a whole new application)
steps.time_estimate: Applying online gives faster processing than other methods
applies_to_rules: Temporary residents: SIN starts with "9" and expires with your immigration documents; you must apply again to extend the expiry date of a temporary SIN
If you already know your SIN, do not reapply — view and print it by signing in to My Service Canada Account (MSCA)
Service Canada no longer issues plastic SIN cards; if a card is lost or damaged, request a Confirmation of SIN letter
If Service Canada cannot issue you a SIN, you may request a temporary tax number (TTN) from the CRA for benefits, credits and filing taxes

steps.title: Apply for BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) after you arrive — and rely on iMED in the meantime
steps.why: All B.C. residents must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP), and if you don't have other medical coverage you are required by BC law to register. Coverage may only start three months after your arrival date in B.C., so you need private coverage for the wait period. At UBC, international students are charged a temporary iMED medical insurance fee when they register for courses; iMED covers you until your MSP coverage begins (likely in November if you arrived in August). Apply for MSP as soon as you arrive — applying online is the easiest and fastest way. Note that coverage depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: Arrival in British Columbia (the three-month wait period starts from your arrival date)
Course registration at UBC, which triggers the temporary iMED insurance charge to your student account
Study permit documentation for your MSP application
steps.cost: MSP: $75/month for students on a study permit ($0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents). Temporary iMED coverage: $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students), plus a $10.54 direct billing fee.
steps.time_estimate: Apply as soon as you arrive; MSP coverage begins about three months after your arrival date in B.C. (November 1, 2026 onward for an August arrival)

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: MSP enrolment is mandatory for everyone residing in B.C., but new residents are only eligible for coverage after a wait period equal to the balance of the month in which residence is established plus two months — so coverage may not start until about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Following up confirms your application was processed and that you complete enrolment via your B.C. Services Card, which is how you receive your Personal Health Number (PHN). Knowing your exact coverage start date tells you how long you must stay on private health insurance so you are not uninsured for doctor visits.
prerequisites: Submitted an Application for MSP Enrolment (online, in person or by mail) after arriving in B.C.
Record of your arrival date in B.C., used to calculate the wait period
Private health care insurance arranged to cover you until MSP coverage begins
ID documents required to complete MSP enrolment and obtain a B.C. Services Card
steps.cost: No application fee; budget for private health insurance premiums covering the wait period
steps.time_estimate: About 15-30 minutes to follow up; coverage typically begins around three months after your arrival date in B.C.
